chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Fazalah, from Aban, from Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik or Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding a man who prays but did not open with the Takbir, will the Takbir of the Ruku' suffice him? He said: No, but he should repeat his prayer if he remembers that he did not say Takbir.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرِ: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' (God is the Greatest), specifically the opening declaration in prayer.
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةُ الرُّكُوعِ: The Takbir said when bowing into the Ruku' position.
key_terms.تُجْزِئُهُ: To suffice or be acceptable for him.
key_terms.حَفِظَ: He remembered or kept in mind.
key_terms.يَفْتَتِحْ: To open or commence (specifically with the opening Takbir).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one forgets the opening Takbir during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal necessity of the opening Takbir as a distinct pillar of prayer, distinguishing it from the Takbir accompanying the bowing. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) specifies that the prayer is invalid if the omission is remembered, emphasizing the structural integrity of the prayer's commencement in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the importance of precise ritual performance, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on adhering to the Prophet's and Imams' detailed guidance in worship.
